mainEntity.name: How do I know if I need a crown or just a filling?

acceptedAnswer.text: The only reliable way to determine whether you need a crown or a filling is through a clinical examination by a qualified dentist. Your dentist will assess the extent of the damage, how much healthy tooth structure remains, and whether there is any underlying infection or nerve involvement. While general guidance can help you understand the factors involved, individual assessment is always required before any treatment recommendation is made.

mainEntity.name: Can a large filling be replaced with another filling, or does it need a crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the condition of the remaining tooth structure. In some cases, a large existing filling can be replaced with another filling if sufficient healthy tooth wall remains. However, if the filling occupies a significant proportion of the tooth, or if the surrounding walls have become thin or weakened, a crown is often the more appropriate long-term option. Your dentist will assess this during your examination and discuss the best approach for your situation.

Crown preparation is usually carried out under local anaesthetic, which means the tooth and surrounding area will be numbed before any work begins. Most patients find the procedure comfortable. After the anaesthetic wears off, some mild sensitivity or soreness around the gum is not unusual and typically settles within a few days. If you experience significant or prolonged discomfort following the procedure, it is advisable to contact your dental practice for guidance.

mainEntity.name: How long does a dental crown last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of a crown varies depending on the material used, the position of the tooth, your bite, and your oral hygiene habits. Well-maintained crowns can last ten years or more, and in many cases considerably longer. Regular dental check-ups allow your dentist to monitor the condition of a crown and identify any early signs of wear or failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it urgent if a filling falls out?

acceptedAnswer.text: A lost filling should be assessed by a dentist as soon as reasonably possible. While it may not always constitute a dental emergency, an exposed tooth is more vulnerable to sensitivity, further decay, and damage. If you experience significant pain, swelling, or visible damage to the tooth, contact your dentist promptly. In the meantime, avoid eating on that side of your mouth and keep the area clean.

mainEntity.name: Can I choose between a filling and a crown?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your dentist will always explain the available treatment options and their likely outcomes, allowing you to make an informed decision. However, clinical factors such as the extent of damage or structural integrity of the tooth may mean that one option is significantly more appropriate than the other. Your dentist's recommendation will be based on what is clinically suitable and in the best long-term interest of your oral health.
